title: Mordheim KB catalogue — catalog/campaign/hired-swords-and-dramatis.yaml
description: The campaign side of hiring: the search procedure, the fee and upkeep of every Hired Sword and Dramatis Persona, their availability and their static eligibility. The character himself — characteristics, equipment, skills and intrinsic rules — belongs to `catalog/hirelings/`, and this catalogue only points at him with `profile_id`. Current-roster, current-hires and warband-variant checks are profile rules evaluated by the application, never inferred from the static lists here; `eligibility_semantics` states that boundary as data.

availability_procedures.description: The procedures that decide whether a character is available to be looked for.

hired_swords.description: The hiring entries of the Hired Swords.

dramatis_personae.description: The hiring entries of the Dramatis Personae. Unlike a Hired Sword, a Dramatis entry may declare no hiring fee when the source hires him by another route (a summoning, a scenario).

effect_ids.description: Effects of this catalogue a warband's own special rules may modify.

availability_procedure.description: One search procedure: a characteristic test that says whether the character can be found.

actor.description: Who searches, e.g. an eligible Hero.

success_when.description: How the roll is compared with the characteristic.

profile_id.description: Profile of `catalog/hirelings/hired-swords/` the entry hires. The profile is never copied here.

upkeep.description: What keeping him costs after every battle, or `null` when the source charges no upkeep (a Hired Sword who serves a single battle, or one the warband does not keep).

availability.description: How the Hired Sword is obtained. `common` is hired from the market list; `construction` and `hero_replacement` are the source's special routes, which a scenario or a warband rule resolves.

hiring_fee.description: What hiring costs, or `null` when the character is not hired with resources at all (a summoning, a scenario reward).

upkeep.description: What keeping him costs after every battle, or `null` when the source charges no upkeep.

availability.description: How the character is obtained: through the search procedure (`procedure_id`) or by one of the source's own special routes (`kind`).

kind.description: Special route, when the character is not looked for on the market.

procedure_id.description: Search procedure of this document that decides whether he is found.

resources_holder.description: A fee or an upkeep, expressed in the resources the source asks for.

resources.description: Which resources and how much of each. The keys are the campaign's resources; a source that charges in treasures or in Campaign Points says so here instead of being converted into crowns.

resource_cost.description: What one resource costs. It is a number, or a formula the source prints as text.

cost.description: Amount of the resource, or the expression the source prints instead of a single number.

eligibility.description: The static eligibility of a hiring entry: which bands may hire the character at all. The lists are the plain cases; `expression` is the boolean form for the cases the lists cannot express, and the two are mutually exclusive.

allow_band_ids.description: Bands that may hire him. When both allow lists are empty there is no positive static filter.

allow_groups.description: Shared band groups that may hire him.

forbid_band_ids.description: Bands that may not hire him. A match here rejects the hire, whatever the allow lists say.

forbid_groups.description: Shared band groups that may not hire him.

expression.description: Complete static predicate for the cases that need boolean composition; when it is present the allow and forbid lists are not used for that entry.

note.description: The source wording of the hiring rule, verbatim, for what the lists cannot express: a warband that 'contains non-humans', a condition that lives in the band's own rules. The lists carry what is modelled and this keeps what is only printed, exactly as `restriction.note` does in the trading post.

eligibility_expression.description: A static eligibility predicate over band ids and shared band groups. Exactly one operator or leaf per node; the operators nest.

semantics.description: The meaning of the fields above, stated as data so the application and the catalogue cannot drift apart: what the lists mean, what the expression is for and which checks are deliberately left to the application. These are editorial statements, not executable rules.

simple_lists.description: How the allow and forbid lists combine.

precedence.description: Which list wins when both match. Currently `forbid`.

expression.description: What the expression form is for.

leaf_fields.description: The fields an expression may test.

operators.description: The operators an expression may use.

dynamic_checks.description: The checks that are deliberately not part of this catalogue because they depend on the current roster, the current Hires or the selected variants.

characteristic.description: Characteristic a search test rolls against, named in full.
